name: THT Conservation Grant
summary: Three-year grant of INR 1 crore, given to two shortlisted organisations for holistic conservation of India's lesser-known species and critical habitats.

eligibility.rule: Operating for 3 years and carrying out direct on-ground conservation projects by 31 March 2025
Averaging at least INR 30 lakhs expenditure over the last three financial years
Being a registered not-for-profit entity in India
Holding registration under Section 12A of the Income-Tax Act
Holding 80G, or Section 35(1)(ii) approval where 80G does not apply
Having an object clause for wildlife and environmental conservation, lesser-known taxa and habitats
Having no political or religious affiliations

documents: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association or Bye-Laws
Income Tax Returns for FY 2023-24 and 2024-25
Audited financials for FY 2022-23 to FY 2024-25

status.quote: Applications for the THT Conservation Grant, THT Action Grant/Action Service Project and THT Research Grant are Closed Now for 2026!

applicant_types.quote: The grant is only open to organisations.

geography.quote: conservation organisations and individuals, who work to conserve India's natural habitats and native species of flora and fauna

access.quote: Applicants who have successfully submitted their applications are screened by external auditors

effort.quote: Applications will only be accepted through the THT Grant's application portal online, on The Habitats Trust website (www.thehabitatstrust.org/grants).
Applicants who have successfully submitted their applications are screened by external auditors, to check if they meet all the eligibility requirements and pre-requisites for the grants.
The Sub-Jury member(s) and THT team visit shortlisted applicants for field level evaluation and verification at the proposed project's sites.
The finalists have to undergo another in-depth level of due diligence.
The finalists are invited to present their projects to the Jury for the final evaluation.

eligibility.quote: The functional existence of the organisation for 3 years, as per the registration certificate, carrying out direct on-ground conservation projects of India's natural habitats and threatened species, must be completed by 31st March 2025.
An average expenditure greater than or equal to INR 30 lakhs over the last three financial years (FY 2022-23, FY 2023-24, and FY 2024- 25) must have been incurred by the organisation.
A CSR-1 certificate must be held by the organisation.

The organisation must be a registered not-for-profit entity in India (i.e., Society, Trust, Section 8 (previously Section 25) company, or a registered institute under Section 35(1)(ii) of the Income-Tax Act, 1961).
Registration under Section 12A of the Income-Tax Act, 1961, must be held by the organisation.

An 80G certificate must be held by the organisation. For institutes where the 80G certificate is not applicable, approval under Section 35(1)(ii) of the Income-Tax Act, 1961, by the Central Government will be considered.

The organisation's object clause in the MoA/Trust Deed must be pertaining to wildlife and environmental conservation, aimed at conserving lesser known taxa and protecting habitats while ensuring economic well being.
No political or religious affiliations are to be held by the organisation applying.

after_award.quote: Bi-annual reports and a final report on the work supported by The Habitats Trust must be submitted by successful applicants as per the reporting cycle and templates provided.
